message: Thanks. I've noted three children, a married couple in the household (five people total), and that you own your home. To narrow down the programmes, I need two more things: which US state do you live in, and roughly how much does your household earn from work in a year, before tax?

Thanks, Massachusetts noted. Totally fine if you don't know exactly. Could you give a rough estimate? Pick the closest range for your household's combined yearly work income before tax: none; $1 to $10,000; $10,000 to $20,000; $20,000 to $30,000; $30,000 to $40,000; $40,000 to $50,000; $50,000 to $60,000; $60,000 to $80,000; $80,000 to $100,000; $100,000 to $150,000; or $150,000 or more. Also, is any of your children under 5, or is anyone pregnant or has a baby under 1?
reply: I don't really know. Our youngest just turned three. No.

message: Got it: your youngest is 3, and no one is pregnant or has a baby under 1. For income, if it's easier, your last tax return shows total wages (or the AGI line) for the year. Otherwise, roughly how many of you work and about what each earns? Also, does anyone get health insurance through a job?
reply: I don't really know. No idea, honestly.

message: No problem. Let's make it simpler: do you and your husband both have paying jobs right now? Is either of you self-employed? And is your household's total in bank accounts and investments under $20,000, or more than that?

Thanks, that helps. I still need a ballpark on pay, since it decides most of these programmes. Could you look at a recent pay stub, or tell me each of your rough annual salaries or hourly rates? Even "under $60,000" or "over $100,000" combined would help. Also, do either of you get health insurance through your job?
reply: I don't really know. No idea, honestly.

summary: Household: Massachusetts, married couple plus three children (youngest is 3), owns home, savings and investments about $89,100. Household income from work is unknown; the person could not estimate it or check a pay stub, and did not say whether either of them has employer health insurance. Recommended, with a caseworker to confirm: school_meals (Massachusetts offers free meals to public school students regardless of income; confirm the children attend public school), medicaid and chip (MassHealth children's coverage, which has high income limits in MA and no asset test for children; confirm income), and ctc (refundable portion, which depends on earned income above $2,500; confirm). Not recommended: TANF and SSI (savings are too high; no one is known to be disabled or 65+). SNAP and WIC were not recommended because income is unknown and they depend on it; a caseworker should check them once income is known. EITC and ACA premium tax credit also depend on income and were not recommended without it. Caseworker should get an income figure first and then recheck SNAP, WIC, EITC and ACA.
